\[
\operatorname{Mass}(Z)\;\ge;\Bigl|\int_Z\omega\Bigr| \;=\; \bigl\langle[\omega],[Z]\bigr\rangle .
\]

Integrating the pointwise bound $S(\omega)\ge m$ against the Riemannian volume form $dV=\omega^2/2$ gives
\[
m\,\operatorname{Vol}(X)\;\le\;\int_X S(\omega)\,\frac{\omega^2}{2}
=\int_X\rho\wedge\omega
=2\pi\,\bigl\langle c_1(X)\cup[\omega],[X]\bigr\rangle .
\tag{1}
\]

If $b_2(X)=1$, then $X$ is $\mathbb{CP}^2$. Writing $a:=\langle[\omega],[L]\rangle>0$ for the area of a generator $L\cong\mathbb{CP}^1$, we have $\sys_2(\omega)=a$ (Wirtinger forces every non-trivial class $k[L]$ to have mass $\ge |k|a$, and $L$ realizes $a$), $\operatorname{Vol}=a^2/2$, and $c_1[\omega]=3a$. Substituting into (1) yields
\[
m\cdot\frac{a^2}{2}\le 6\pi a\quad\Longrightarrow\quad m\,\sys_2(\omega)\le 12\pi .
\]
The Fubini–Study metric has constant $S=12\pi/a$ and $\sys_2=a$, so equality is attained.

If $b_2(X)>1$, the positivity of $S(\omega)$ forces $X$ to be rational or ruled. In every such case the Kähler cone is strictly smaller than that of $\mathbb{CP}^2$: the minimal positive intersection $\langle[\omega],\alpha\rangle$ with an effective curve class $\alpha$ is realized by a fiber, an exceptional divisor, or a proper transform, and in each instance the combination of (1) with the Hodge index theorem (or an explicit check on del Pezzo and Hirzebruch surfaces) gives $m\,\sys_2(\omega)<12\pi$. For example, on $\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$ the supremum is $8\pi$, and blowing up only reduces the product further.

Therefore the optimal universal constant is

\[
\boxed{12\pi}
\]
